newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's southern rebels ponder next move.
newsitem.headline: Albania's southern rebels ponder next move.

text.p: Rebels in control of southern Albania were to meet on Friday to decide their next move after embattled President Sali Berisha ignored their ultimatum to quit.

The rebels blame Berisha for not stopping shady pyramid savings schemes which collapsed earlier this year, bankrupting thousands of families and sparking an armed uprising that brought Albania close to the abyss.
In Tirana, a regular night time security patrol of tanks, armoured vehicles and police vans was preceded by several sustained bursts of automatic weapons fire.

It was not clear what had caused the shooting, which was more than usually heavy and broke out after a 7:00 pm curfew went into force, but witnesses reported seeing an ambulance move along one central Tirana street.
As part of efforts to restore order ater weekks of chaos during which army barracks were looted of thousands of guns, Tirana international airport reopened on Thursday for the first time in a week.

Authorities said they had moved in special forces to ensure the airport's security. About 30 foreigners left for Sofia on an Albanian Airlines flight, while an Italian air force transport plane brought in up to 90 Albanian refugees sent back by Italy as criminal suspects.
More than 10,000 Albanians fleeing the civil strife have escaped across the Adriatic in leaky boats to Italy. But the Italian authorites allege that many are involved in criminal activities.

In the Italian port of Brindisi, police said an Albanian gunman whose photograph appeared in newspapers around the world was arrested on Thursday on suspicion of running an illegal immigration racket.
The man, named as Despoti Clirim, 27, was photographed in the Albanian port of Durres earlier pointing a rifle at crowds of frightened people desperate to board ships leaving the country.

Italy, which has been at the forefront of diplomatic efforts to restore order in Albania, said the country's Prime Minister, Bashkim Fino, would meet European Union foreign ministers next Tuesday in Rome.
The meeting would come the day after EU foreign ministers go to Brussels to hear from an EU fact-finding mission which visited Albania to assess the situation there.

Albania has asked Italy to help it to re-equip its army and police force, disarmed and demoralised after the unrest, but Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said there were no plans for an imminent military intervention.
Leaders from 13 rebel-held towns in the south, who have have threatened to set up their own presidential council, were due to meet in the town of Tepelene.
One rebel leader has proposed sending armed men to Tirana to put Berisha under house arrest, but this found little support from others in the south.
Political leaders, now part of the all-party government charged with organising elections by June, have come out against using force to remove Berisha, saying the democratic process will decide.
"We do not support any military move to overthrow Berisha. We think he can and should be removed by legal, peaceful means," said Social Democrat vice chairman Paskal Milo.
The Rome-based U.N. World Food Programme said it had sent a team to Tirana on a one-week mission to assess Albania's relief needs.

Albanian Agriculure Minister Haxhi Aliko said the food situation was difficult after weeks of looting but there was no need to panic. He said traders should not to exploit the state of emergency to increase their profits.
